title: OneLake Shortcut Authorization Failed: Fixing Cross-Workspace 403 Errors
summary: A community troubleshooting walkthrough for a 403 'OneLake shortcut authorization failed' error that appears when a lakehouse shortcut spans two workspaces. It maps the error to three distinct root causes and gives a matching fix for each.
audience: Fabric admins and lakehouse owners who see shortcut access denied errors in a multi-workspace setup and need to know which of several possible causes applies to them.
why_it_matters: Cross-workspace shortcut authorization failures can look identical in the UI while stemming from unrelated causes (identity delegation, missing data-plane roles, credential rotation, or a UI-only false positive), so a fast differential checklist shortens what would otherwise be a multi-cause guessing exercise.
takeaways: A 403 on a cross-workspace OneLake shortcut is often an identity-mode misconfiguration, not a missing permission.
Control-plane workspace roles (e.g. Viewer) and OneLake data-plane security roles are separate grants; both must be present.
Row-level security can produce a 403-looking preview failure in the UI even when the underlying query succeeds.
External ADLS Gen2 shortcuts have their own credential-expiry failure mode, distinct from internal OneLake shortcuts.

claims.text: A cross-workspace OneLake shortcut can return a 403 authorization error when the source lakehouse's SQL analytics endpoint is set to a fixed or delegated identity instead of user identity, which blocks single sign-on passthrough between the two workspaces.

Setting the source lakehouse's SQL analytics endpoint identity mode to 'user identity' is reported to resolve cross-workspace shortcut 403 errors caused by blocked SSO passthrough, provided the calling user also holds at least Viewer on the source workspace.

Workspace-level control-plane roles (e.g. Viewer) and OneLake data-plane security role assignments are separate grants; a user can hold a workspace role yet still be denied at the shortcut target path without an explicit OneLake data-access role.
After assigning a OneLake security read role on a shortcut path, the post reports an observed propagation delay of roughly two to three minutes before access takes effect.

External ADLS Gen2 shortcuts can fail authorization when SAS tokens or account keys used as the shortcut credential expire or rotate, a distinct failure mode from internal OneLake-to-OneLake shortcuts that rely on identity passthrough.

The post recommends configuring a Fabric workspace identity (a service principal) with the Storage Blob Data Reader Azure RBAC role on the target ADLS Gen2 account for external shortcuts, instead of fixed SAS/account-key credentials, to avoid future credential-expiry failures.

Row-level security applied to a shortcut's target table can cause the Lakehouse Explorer preview pane to show a 403-style failure even though a direct SQL query (e.g. a SELECT TOP 10) against the same shortcut succeeds, indicating the failure is a UI preview limitation rather than a real authorization gap.
The post notes reports of P-SKU capacities showing incompatibility with firewalled ADLS Gen2 access for shortcuts, unless Trusted Workspace Access is configured.
